title: Free lessons at TCU and his American studies doctorate
summary: Cecil Brower and others sent him to the TCU piano teacher, who gave free lessons after hearing him. His degree was in English, with a dissertation in American studies on jazz.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, this Cecil Brower that we're talking about, the one who is the leading hillbilly violinist right now in Nashville, making more records than anybody in the area of hillbilly music is, make no mistake about it, a classical violinist. No doubt about it, and he was the one, he and Kenneth, who kept, and Marvin, studying out at TCU, who told the people about me and had me go out there. The first day I went out there, I was scared to death, and the teacher had me come in and asked me to play the man I love, and I was trying to play it like I imagined it would be written. And the teacher saw at once what was going on and stopped me and had me even play other things, and arranged to give me free lessons in the afternoon, and that's how I broke away into the scholastic life. Your degree is in English though, is it not? Yes. I wrote my dissertation though on June of July. stuff
